cases.statement: One person: the female proband of Family 19 in the 30413001 survey. Table 1 lists no other affected relatives for this family.

people.label: proband (Family 19)
people.zygosity_or_genotype: not reported (female; zygosity not stated for this person)
people.key_phenotypes: very early onset at 6 years with severe cardiac failure (sentence cites reference [22], the Family 19 source)

quotes.quote: One patient had very early onset at the age of six years, with severe cardiac failure similar to that in males [22].
Yamamoto K., Ootsuka Y., Miyake K., et al, 2013, A girl patient of Danon disease with a novel LAMP-2 mutation diagnosed by severe heart failure (translation), J. Jpn. Pediatr. Soc.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Per-person clinical detail is limited; the survey reports that all patients had cardiomyopathy (cohort-level). Testing of other genes is not reported.

segregation.statement: Table 1 lists no affected relatives for this family; relatives' genotypes are not reported. The survey reports no manifesting mothers among the four female probands (cohort-level).

quotes.quote: | Manifesting mothers of the probands, n (%) | 10/16 (63%) | 0/4 (0%) |

de_novo.statement: The authors state that all four female probands (Families 13, 18, 19 and 20 in Table 1) had de novo mutations, but they do not say which parents were tested, with what result, or whether parentage was confirmed.

quotes.quote: All four female probands had de novo mutations.
Interestingly, the mothers of the probands from 10 families had no cardiac involvement and no mutations in LAMP-2.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Single-base substitution predicted to create a stop codon (p.(Leu141Ter)); Table 1 places it in exon 4 and labels it 'Stop codon'. Authors attribute female disease to haploinsufficiency from a heterozygous null mutation.

quotes.quote: All mutations were either nonsense or frame-shift mutations that are predicted to cause truncation of the protein, except for the exon 6 skipping mutation in Family 5.
Therefore, we attributed these results to a 50% reduction in LAMP-2, i.e., ‘LAMP-2 haploinsufficiency’, caused by a heterozygous null mutation in LAMP-2 in female patients [5].

population_data_in_papers.statement: Cohort-level statement: none of the survey's mutations was found in 100 Japanese controls.

quotes.quote: On screening 100 Japanese controls, the same mutations were not found.

concerns: Survey table only; the case description is in the source reference listed in Table 1, which is not in this batch.
The de novo statement covers all four female probands as a group; no parental genotypes or parentage testing are given for this family.
The survey's sentence 'X chromosomes were heterozygous in all 19 families' is unclear and is not used here as zygosity evidence.

The early-onset (6 years) severe heart failure is linked to Family 19 only through citation [22], which Table 1 gives as the Family 19 source; [22] is a Japanese-language society report not in this batch.

30413001 contradicts itself on recurrent variants: the text says Family 11 and Family 15 share c.877C > T, while Table 1 lists c.877C>T for Families 10 and 14, c.371_372 delCA for Family 11 and c.56T>C for Family 15.
30413001 gives two different counts for families whose mothers or relatives tested negative (eight families in Results, 10 families in Discussion) and does not say which families these are.
30413001 states no transcript and no protein change; c. numbering cannot be checked against NM_002294.3 from this paper alone.
notes_for_panel: 30413001 is a nationwide questionnaire survey; per-family information is limited to Table 1 (site, cDNA change, effect on mRNA, affected relatives, source reference). It gives no transcript, no protein change and no per-person phenotype table.
